current.name: Fmdac
current.description: Fmdac 0.9, identity FM-1_969. Four kit tracks, T1 to T4. A track is a whole kit of eight lanes, and all four kits play together. SELECT picks the kit. On HOME the selected kit is marked, and pressing HOME again chooses MIDI or a drum machine for that kit. A MIDI kit is silent locally and still sends MIDI. SEL on a drum kit opens 808, 909, CR-78, and SDS. SEL on a MIDI kit opens that kit's map list. SELECT moves through the list, SEL picks, and HOME closes the list and leaves the kit as it was. On the step grid, a black key picks a lane and K4 is the lane. Off the grid the keys play the kit: C kick, D snare, F# closed hat. A MIDI kit with a scale other than the map plays that scale from the keys. The ARP page keeps the sine tone. Each kit has its own map, MIDI channel, level, and drum character. The channels start at 10, 11, 12, and 13. On a drum kit, EDIT is the kit editor: tune, decay, tone, and drop, then the lane levels. On a MIDI kit, EDIT is the scale (map, chromatic, major, minor, pentatonic, or dorian), then the lane notes, then the map. K1 starts with GM, TR-909, TR-707, TR-727, TR-08, Volca Beats, and Hammerhead, and K2 opens the next page of that chart. Those are the published MIDI notes of those instruments. Hammerhead there is the grouped list. HAMR2 is the same eight notes in the order the OCTACHRON author posted. After those seven, the list and K1 continue through the AUv3 app maps: AR-909, Axon 2, Blip Box, Dadamachines Automat, Digistix, DM1/DM2/Drumlab, DrumComputer, EGDR 606, EGDR 808, EGDR 909, FAC Drumkit, General MIDI 8, General MIDI 16, Koala Sampler 2x8, Koala Sampler 4x4, Korg Gadget Amsterdam, Bilbao, Gladstone, London, Recife, and Tokyo, MV08, NS2 Slate, Pure Acid Drums, Ruismaker, Ruismaker FM, SDS-X, Sitala, Splat-to-Clat, VA Drum SM, VA Drum 2 808, VA Drum 2 909, and Vatanator. The names on the screen are short, and the bottom line names the app. The notes are the public chart that matches the lists the OCTACHRON author posted. General MIDI 8 and 16 use channel 10. The other app maps use channel 1. A lane the chart leaves empty stays silent and sends no MIDI. Sitala is the chromatic pads from 36 to 51. OneShot and Tekno are not included, because those apps do not publish a fixed note chart. This file does not contain every preset stored inside the OCTACHRON app. TR-707 and TR-727 use their shared notes 35 through 51. The original TR-808 has no MIDI, so the 808-style map is the TR-08 chart. Volca Beats part level is CC 40 through 49. HOME sets the level of each kit. The sounding drums are four voices shared by the kits, so a second kick retriggers the first. SEQ is the step grid, then a song chain of four patterns. REC while stopped quantizes a take of one, two, or four bars across at most four patterns and sets the BPM. A song saved by 0.8 loads as the factory kits. It is not a looper. FX runs Prophet VS, DX7, SP-1200, Emulator II, or S950. While the computer streams audio to the FM-1, that audio is converted on the way to the headphones. Playback at 48 kHz is resampled to the headphone clock. When nothing is streaming, the headphones hear the FM-1's own mix. No sample ROMs.
